dossier.scp_unleashed.109.title: Infinite Canteen
dossier.scp_unleashed.109.caption: SCP-109 at intake, beside its evidence tag. It was full then too.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-109 is kept in a standard storage container when it is not issued. It may be signed out as a drinking water supply and must be returned at the end of each shift.
While SCP-109 is seated in a canteen tap on Site plumbing, no further precautions are needed. Taps are inspected weekly and their output is logged.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-109 is a dented aluminium army canteen of Second World War pattern, carried in a worn olive canvas cover with a wire belt hook. Its cap hangs from the neck on a short chain.
SCP-109 is always full. Water drawn from it is cool, clean and drinkable, and no amount of drinking or pouring lowers its level.
Seated in a canteen tap, SCP-109 will supply a pressurized pipe network for as long as the network takes water. The tap's fittings, not SCP-109, set the limit.

page.title: Addendum 109-1: Flow Tests
text: Test 109-02: SCP-109 was inverted over a floor drain for six hours. It poured steadily and remained full.
Test 109-05: SCP-109 was seated in a prototype tap on a pressurized network. Output rose until the fittings could carry no more.
Test 109-08: a researcher whose coat had caught fire took a long drink from SCP-109. The flames went out. %rThe researcher has asked not to be set on fire again.%r

page.title: Addendum 109-2: Provenance
page.text: SCP-109 has no recovery record. It was handed to a reader of this file by the individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects, who asked only that it be given a proper tap. See field notes.

jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp109_canteen.1: SCP-109 is a battered army canteen of Second World War pattern in a worn canvas cover. However much you drink or pour, it stays full.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp109_canteen.2: Hold use to drink. A drink puts out any fire on you and leaves you a little refreshed. Use it on a cauldron to fill the cauldron, or hold an empty bottle in your other hand to fill the bottle.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp109_canteen.3: It cannot be crafted. Recover the SCP-109 dossier from an Archive Terminal and break its seal; a stranger in Foundation dress hands the canteen over in person. It fits in a storage container.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp109_canteen_ta: A plumbing cradle made at the Advanced Materials Bench. Use SCP-109 on it to seat the canteen, and take it back with an empty hand. Breaking the tap drops the canteen.
While SCP-109 is seated, pipes on any side but the front draw endless water from it, up to %s mB/s in total. A pressurizer on the pipe network moves the water, just as it does for a tank.

Buckets, bottles and other containers fill straight from a seated tap. The lamp lights while the canteen is seated and the sight glass bubbles while water flows. Comparators read 7 while seated and 15 while flowing.
